transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I, uh... I guess I'm here because of my face. It's... the left side. It just looks crooked. Messed up. I try not to think about it, but I can't. At work—I work in a warehouse—or when I go to salsa night... I just feel like everyone is staring at it. They say they don't see it, but... I know they do.
Do you believe that your face is truly crooked or distorted, even though others say they don't see it?

Yeah. I mean... I know what I see in the mirror. It *is* crooked. 

I just... I can't stop thinking about it. Like I said, even if the guys at the warehouse or people at salsa say they don't notice anything... I know they do. They see how messed up it is. They just... they just don't want to say it to my face.
Do you think your face looks abnormal in any other way besides being crooked?
Uh... no. Not really. Just... just that it's crooked. I don't really notice anything else. Just the left side.
Do you think about how your face looks every day, or does it come and go?

Uh... every day. Yeah. It doesn't really go away. 

Like I said, I just... I can't stop thinking about it. How crooked it is. Whether I'm pulling orders at the warehouse or... wherever. It's just always on my mind. I just know people are noticing it.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or comparing your face to others, to try to fix or get reassurance about how your face looks?

Yeah... I guess so. Like, at work... before I go back out on the inventory floor, I usually stop in the bathroom. Just to check the mirror. 

I... I try to fix my cap, or I just end up rubbing at that same spot on my face. Over and over. I guess I do it a lot, because... sometimes I'm late getting back out there. My picking numbers fall behind, and my boss gets on me about it again. So... yeah. I do that.
Does this concern about your face make it hard for you to focus, interact with others, or do your job well?

Yeah. It does. I mean... I already mentioned my boss. I've been written up a few times because my orders get delayed. And... I don't really go out much anymore. 

I used to play soccer, go to salsa nights... even just family stuff. But I've been skipping all of it. I just... I don't want to deal with people looking at me. Or taking pictures. It's just easier to stay home.
Do you feel distressed or anxious when you can’t check your face, or when you’re reminded of how it looks?

Um... I don't really know. I'm not sure. I usually just go to the bathroom and check when I need to, so... I haven't really thought about what happens if I can't. It just... bothers me, I guess. That's all.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like soccer or salsa nights?

I don't know. Maybe. I just... I told you, I stay home more now. It's not that I don't like those things anymore, I just... don't want to go. I don't really know about feeling hopeless. I'm just... tired of it all, I guess.
Do you ever feel like the way your face looks is somehow connected to other things, like people talking about you or trying to send you messages through how your face appears?
No... no, nothing like that. I don't think people are sending me messages or anything. I just... I just know how I look. That's it.
How long has your concern about the left side of your face been bothering you?
I don't really know. Um... a while, I guess. I haven't exactly kept track of when it started or anything. It's just... been bothering me. I'm not sure how long.
Can you think back and tell me approximately how long you have been feeling bothered by how the left side of your face looks?
I just said I don't really know. Um... maybe a couple of years? I don't remember exactly when it started. It's just... always there now.
Do you feel bothered by how your face looks every day, and does it stay on your mind most of the day, even when you're trying to focus on other things?

Yeah... pretty much every day. It's hard to ignore. I just... I can't stop thinking about how the left side of my face looks crooked. Like it's just messed up. Even when I'm at the warehouse working, or... or if I go to salsa night. It's always on my mind. I feel like everyone is noticing it, even when people tell me they don't see anything wrong. It just doesn't go away.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (crooked left side of the face), repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, touching the face), and significant distress and impairment in functioning (e.g., avoiding social activities, work performance issues) are consistent with body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22). No evidence was found to support other candidates such as persistent somatic symptom disorder (F34.8).
